\chapter{Learning Theory — CCE}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Minimax.CCE
\section{Overview}

This module develops the theory of \emph{coarse correlated equilibria} (CCE)
for finite two-player games.  It introduces joint distributions over action
profiles, defines (approximate) CCE in terms of one-sided deviation utilities,
constructs the empirical joint distribution from a sequence of mixed-strategy
plays, and proves the main result: if both players run no-regret algorithms
with per-round external regret at most $\varepsilon$, then their empirical
joint distribution is an $\varepsilon$-CCE.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Two-player finite game]
\lean{Game}
\label{Game}
\leanok
A finite two-player game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column actions, specified
by a row utility function $u_r : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \times \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$
and a column utility function $u_c : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \times \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$.
Both players are utility maximizers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding a zero-sum game]
\lean{ZeroSumGame.toGame}
\label{ZeroSumGame.toGame}
\leanok
\uses{Game, ZeroSumGame}
Given a zero-sum game $G$ with payoff matrix $A$, this embeds it into the
general two-player framework by setting the row utility to $A$ and the column
utility to $-A$, so that both players are maximizers of their respective
utilities.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Joint distribution over action profiles]
\lean{JointDistribution}
\label{JointDistribution}
\leanok
A joint distribution $\sigma$ on $\mathrm{Fin}\,M \times \mathrm{Fin}\,N$ is a
nonnegative function $\sigma_{ij} \ge 0$ satisfying
$\sum_{i,j} \sigma_{ij} = 1$.  It represents a correlated distribution over
pure action profiles of the two players.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Row marginal]
\lean{JointDistribution.rowMarginal}
\label{JointDistribution.rowMarginal}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution}
The row marginal of $\sigma$ at row action $i$ is
$\sigma^{\mathrm{row}}_i = \sum_{j} \sigma_{ij}$,
i.e.\ the probability that the row player plays $i$ under $\sigma$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Column marginal]
\lean{JointDistribution.colMarginal}
\label{JointDistribution.colMarginal}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution}
The column marginal of $\sigma$ at column action $j$ is
$\sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_j = \sum_{i} \sigma_{ij}$,
i.e.\ the probability that the column player plays $j$ under $\sigma$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Row marginals are nonnegative]
\lean{JointDistribution.rowMarginal_nonneg}
\label{JointDistribution.rowMarginal_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution, JointDistribution.rowMarginal}
\difficulty{1}
For any joint distribution $\sigma$ and row action $i$,
$\sigma^{\mathrm{row}}_i \ge 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Column marginals are nonnegative]
\lean{JointDistribution.colMarginal_nonneg}
\label{JointDistribution.colMarginal_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution, JointDistribution.colMarginal}
\difficulty{1}
For any joint distribution $\sigma$ and column action $j$,
$\sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_j \ge 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Row marginals sum to one]
\lean{JointDistribution.rowMarginal_sum_one}
\label{JointDistribution.rowMarginal_sum_one}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution, JointDistribution.rowMarginal}
\difficulty{1}
The row marginals form a valid probability distribution:
$\sum_{i} \sigma^{\mathrm{row}}_i = 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Column marginals sum to one]
\lean{JointDistribution.colMarginal_sum_one}
\label{JointDistribution.colMarginal_sum_one}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution, JointDistribution.colMarginal}
\difficulty{2}
The column marginals form a valid probability distribution:
$\sum_{j} \sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_j = 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Row expected utility]
\lean{JointDistribution.rowExpectedUtility}
\label{JointDistribution.rowExpectedUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution}
The row player's expected utility under $\sigma$ in game $G$ is
$\sum_{i,j} \sigma_{ij} \cdot u_r(i,j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Column expected utility]
\lean{JointDistribution.colExpectedUtility}
\label{JointDistribution.colExpectedUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution}
The column player's expected utility under $\sigma$ in game $G$ is
$\sum_{i,j} \sigma_{ij} \cdot u_c(i,j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Row deviation utility]
\lean{JointDistribution.rowDeviationUtility}
\label{JointDistribution.rowDeviationUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution, JointDistribution.colMarginal}
The row player's expected utility from unilaterally deviating to the fixed
pure action $i'$, while the column player keeps $\sigma$'s column marginal:
$\sum_{j} \sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_j \cdot u_r(i', j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Column deviation utility]
\lean{JointDistribution.colDeviationUtility}
\label{JointDistribution.colDeviationUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution, JointDistribution.rowMarginal}
The column player's expected utility from unilaterally deviating to the fixed
pure action $j'$, while the row player keeps $\sigma$'s row marginal:
$\sum_{i} \sigma^{\mathrm{row}}_i \cdot u_c(i, j')$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coarse correlated equilibrium]
\lean{IsCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium}
\label{IsCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution, JointDistribution.rowDeviationUtility, JointDistribution.rowExpectedUtility, JointDistribution.colDeviationUtility, JointDistribution.colExpectedUtility}
A joint distribution $\sigma$ is a \emph{coarse correlated equilibrium} (CCE)
of game $G$ if neither player can improve their expected utility by committing
in advance to any fixed pure action: for all $i'$,
$\mathrm{rowDevUtil}(\sigma, G, i') \le \mathrm{rowExpUtil}(\sigma, G)$, and
for all $j'$, $\mathrm{colDevUtil}(\sigma, G, j') \le \mathrm{colExpUtil}(\sigma, G)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-coarse correlated equilibrium]
\lean{IsApproxCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium}
\label{IsApproxCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution, JointDistribution.rowDeviationUtility, JointDistribution.rowExpectedUtility, JointDistribution.colDeviationUtility, JointDistribution.colExpectedUtility}
A joint distribution $\sigma$ is an \emph{$\varepsilon$-coarse correlated
equilibrium} ($\varepsilon$-CCE) of game $G$ if each player's gain from any
unilateral pure deviation is at most $\varepsilon$: for all $i'$,
$\mathrm{rowDevUtil}(\sigma, G, i') \le \mathrm{rowExpUtil}(\sigma, G) + \varepsilon$,
and similarly for the column player.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Exact CCE implies approximate CCE]
\lean{IsCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium.toApprox}
\label{IsCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium.toApprox}
\leanok
\uses{Game, IsCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium, IsApproxCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium, JointDistribution, productDistribution}
\difficulty{2}
If $\sigma$ is an exact CCE of $G$ and $\varepsilon \ge 0$, then $\sigma$ is
also an $\varepsilon$-CCE of $G$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Product distribution]
\lean{productDistribution}
\label{productDistribution}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution, MixedStrategy}
Given mixed strategies $p$ for the row player and $q$ for the column player,
the product (independent) joint distribution assigns to each profile $(i,j)$
the probability $p_i \cdot q_j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Product distribution row marginal]
\lean{productDistribution_rowMarginal}
\label{productDistribution_rowMarginal}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution.rowMarginal, MixedStrategy, productDistribution}
\difficulty{2}
For the product distribution of $p$ and $q$, the row marginal at $i$ equals
$p_i$ (the original row mixed-strategy weight).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Product distribution column marginal]
\lean{productDistribution_colMarginal}
\label{productDistribution_colMarginal}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution.colMarginal, MixedStrategy, productDistribution}
\difficulty{2}
For the product distribution of $p$ and $q$, the column marginal at $j$ equals
$q_j$ (the original column mixed-strategy weight).
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Empirical joint distribution]
\lean{empiricalJoint}
\label{empiricalJoint}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution, MixedStrategy}
Given $T > 0$ rounds of play in which the row player uses mixed strategy $p_t$
and the column player uses $q_t$, the empirical joint distribution assigns to
each profile $(i,j)$ the time-averaged probability
$\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} (p_t)_i \cdot (q_t)_j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical joint row marginal]
\lean{empiricalJoint_rowMarginal}
\label{empiricalJoint_rowMarginal}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution.rowMarginal, MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint}
\difficulty{3}
The row marginal of the empirical joint distribution at action $i$ equals the
time-average of the row player's mixed-strategy weights:
$(1/T)\sum_{t} (p_t)_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical joint column marginal]
\lean{empiricalJoint_colMarginal}
\label{empiricalJoint_colMarginal}
\leanok
\uses{JointDistribution.colMarginal, MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint}
\difficulty{3}
The column marginal of the empirical joint distribution at action $j$ equals
the time-average of the column player's mixed-strategy weights:
$(1/T)\sum_{t} (q_t)_j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical utility sum factorization]
\lean{empiricalJoint_sum_prob_mul}
\label{empiricalJoint_sum_prob_mul}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint}
\difficulty{4}
For any function $f : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$,
the sum $\sum_{i,j} \sigma_{ij} \cdot f(i,j)$ over the empirical joint
distribution equals the time-average
$(1/T)\sum_{t}\sum_{i,j}(p_t)_i(q_t)_j f(i,j)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical row expected utility]
\lean{empiricalJoint_rowExpectedUtility}
\label{empiricalJoint_rowExpectedUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution.rowExpectedUtility, MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint, empiricalJoint_sum_prob_mul}
\difficulty{1}
The row player's expected utility under the empirical joint distribution equals
the time-average of the per-round bilinear utilities:
\[
  \mathrm{rowExpUtil}(\sigma^{\mathrm{emp}}, G) =
  \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t}\sum_{i,j}(p_t)_i\,(q_t)_j\,u_r(i,j).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical column expected utility]
\lean{empiricalJoint_colExpectedUtility}
\label{empiricalJoint_colExpectedUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution.colExpectedUtility, MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint, empiricalJoint_sum_prob_mul}
\difficulty{1}
The column player's expected utility under the empirical joint distribution
equals the time-average of the per-round bilinear column utilities:
\[
  \mathrm{colExpUtil}(\sigma^{\mathrm{emp}}, G) =
  \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t}\sum_{i,j}(p_t)_i\,(q_t)_j\,u_c(i,j).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical row deviation utility]
\lean{empiricalJoint_rowDeviationUtility}
\label{empiricalJoint_rowDeviationUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution.rowDeviationUtility, MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint, empiricalJoint_colMarginal}
\difficulty{3}
The row player's deviation utility for pure action $i'$ in the empirical
distribution equals the time-average utility of always playing $i'$:
\[
  \mathrm{rowDevUtil}(\sigma^{\mathrm{emp}}, G, i') =
  \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t}\sum_{j}(q_t)_j\,u_r(i',j).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical column deviation utility]
\lean{empiricalJoint_colDeviationUtility}
\label{empiricalJoint_colDeviationUtility}
\leanok
\uses{Game, JointDistribution.colDeviationUtility, MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint, empiricalJoint_rowMarginal}
\difficulty{3}
The column player's deviation utility for pure action $j'$ in the empirical
distribution equals the time-average utility of always playing $j'$:
\[
  \mathrm{colDevUtil}(\sigma^{\mathrm{emp}}, G, j') =
  \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t}\sum_{i}(p_t)_i\,u_c(i,j').
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[No-regret play yields an approximate CCE]
\lean{empiricalJoint_isApproxCCE}
\label{empiricalJoint_isApproxCCE}
\leanok
\uses{Game, IsApproxCoarseCorrelatedEquilibrium, MixedStrategy, empiricalJoint, empiricalJoint_rowDeviationUtility, empiricalJoint_rowExpectedUtility, empiricalJoint_colDeviationUtility, empiricalJoint_colExpectedUtility}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a two-player game, $T > 0$, and let $p_t$, $q_t$ be the mixed
strategies played at round $t$ by the row and column players respectively.
Suppose that for every pure row deviation $i'$,
\[
  \sum_{t}\sum_{j}(q_t)_j u_r(i',j)
  - \sum_{t}\sum_{i,j}(p_t)_i(q_t)_j u_r(i,j) \le \varepsilon T,
\]
and similarly for every column deviation $j'$ using $u_c$.
Then the empirical joint distribution is an $\varepsilon$-CCE of $G$.
\end{theorem}
